body: Regis Le Bris makes no changes from the 1-1 draw with Brentford. Former Arsenal midfielder Granit Xhaka captains Sunderland as usual. Former Spurs defender Kevin Danso is in the centre of defence.

Mikel Arteta also keeps the same XI from the win against Chelsea. Former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimarães is spared the wrath of the Stadium of Light to start with – he’s on the bench. Max Dowman is absent after playing for Arsenal’s under-21s in their defeat to Chelsea this afternoon.
It is goalless between Tottenham and Everton a few minutes into the second half. Thierno Barry has just threatened an opener.

Yes, there is more Premier League action today. Arsenal are looking to maintain their 100% start to the season as champions as they take on Sunderland at a ground where they were held to a 2-2 draw last season. Mikel Arteta’s side were in Italy in midweek, escaping from Naples with a 1-0 win, while their hosts on Wearside this evening also won 1-0 at home to Hull in the Carabao Cup.

articles.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund beat Paderborn 3-0. Freiburg lead on goal difference after 5-0 win. Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga.
body: Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight.
Nmecha came off the bench to score twice, wrapping up victory for the hosts with a stunning late bicycle kick.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made a surprise for his first match since picking up an ankle injury at the World Cup and told Sky Germany he kept his comeback under wraps. “We just hadn’t communicated that much yet because I didn’t want to,” Schlotterbeck said, adding “I missed it terribly. It was a serious injury but I’m glad to be back now.”

Freiburg thumped a poor Borussia Mönchengladbach 5-0 at home to climb to the top. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanovic netted twice each and Maximilian Eggestein added a late fifth as the hosts sent Gladbach, who finished with 10 men, to the foot of the table.

articles.title: Missouri coach blasts Kansas over slavery references after Border War win
articles.summary: Tigers beat Kansas 38-21 in historic Border War. Rivalry has roots in pre-Civil War slavery conflict. Drinkwitz says buildup left him ‘embarrassed’ The latest edition of the Border War between Missouri and Kansas turned out to be a mere skirmish for a half.
body: Robert Woodyard Jr produced back-to-back turnovers soon after the break, and Austin Simmons and the potent Tigers offense turned them into touchdowns, helping No 23 Missouri break open a tie game and roll to a 38-21 victory Friday night.

Jamal Roberts ran for 125 yards and a touchdown, and Donovan Olugbode and Cayden Lee caught TD passes, as the Tigers (2-0) beat their biggest rival for the fifth straight time in their first trip across the state line since 29 October 2005.

“The things that we gave them were undisciplined penalties, special teams were not good tonight in any form or facet, but we overcame it,” Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz said, “and that’s what you have to do on the road.”

That’s not all Drinkwitz had to say, though He took umbrage with the way Kansas leaned into the historic nature of the rivalry, which began as an armed conflict over the issue of slavery along the state line in the years leading up to the Civil War.

articles.title: 'Absolute joke' to be worried - Mitchell on England's response
articles.summary: England produce dominant second-half performance to comfortably defeat Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the opening game of the new WXV Global Series.
body: The world champions, playing their first game since winning a record eighth successive Women's Six Nations title in May, were made to work for victory in Salford after trailing at half-time for the first time since 2020.
The Wallaroos led 10-5 at the break, with player of the match Abi Burton scoring England's only try in an error-strewn first half.

John Mitchell's side responded emphatically after the interval, scoring seven tries to quickly put any prospect of a shock defeat to bed and extend their record winning run to 39 matches in front of a crowd of 9,251.
The England head coach described the fixture as "a good pre-season game" after it kicked off the 2026-27 season for his players.

articles.title: Norris takes Madrid pole with 'gorgeous' lap
articles.summary: Lando Norris takes a superb pole position for McLaren at the Spanish Grand Prix, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
body: "Oh, what a lap, gorgeous," said an ecstatic Norris after pipping world championship leader Antonelli by just 0.011 seconds. "Oh, that might be my best one."
Verstappen was 0.140secs off the pace, as all three moved ahead of Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari in Madrid.
The seven-time champion had held the top spot after the first runs in the final session.
Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc was fifth, ahead of Mercedes' George Russell and the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri.

articles.title: Stunning US fightback sets up Solheim Cup singles showdown
articles.summary: Europe and the United States will head into Sunday's decisive Solheim Cup singles level on points after a breathtaking rearguard action by the Americans in a nail-biting afternoon fourball session.
body: With the light fading on the Bernardus course in the Netherlands, Jennifer Kupcho holed a nerve-shredding putt from the edge of the 18th green to snatch a point and leave the teams tied at 8-8.
Europe had come into the afternoon session with all the momentum, looking to extend an advantage of 7-5 after a tense morning of foursomes.
Fresh from taking down world number one Nelly Korda in the early session, Europe sent out Swedish pair Maja Stark and Linn Grant against in-form Americans Megan Khang and Lauren Coughlin.
And on the very first hole, Stark conjured the shot of the competition so far, her approach to the green on the par four dropping straight into the cup for an eagle.

articles.title: Landa wins stage as Mas moves to brink of Vuelta title
articles.summary: Spanish cycling enjoys a memorable day at the Vuelta a Espana as veteran Mikel Landa wins the penultimate stage and Enric Mas moves to the brink of the title.
body: Veteran Mikel Landa won the penultimate stage and Enric Mas moved to the brink of the title as Spain enjoyed a memorable day at the Vuelta a Espana.
Mas, 31, stretched his lead over four-time winner Primoz Roglic to more than two minutes - with only the final day, a processional stage, to come.
So as long as the Movistar rider stays upright on Sunday, he will become the first Spaniard to win his country's biggest race since Alberto Contador claimed his third Vuelta title in 2014.
Compatriot Landa, meanwhile, earned his first Grand Tour stage win in nine years and his first in the Vuelta since 2015.

articles.title: Aston Villa 1-2 Nottingham Forest: What Glasner and Jesus said
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "I'm really proud of the team's performance and the spirit they showed. We did better after 10 or 15 minutes but we were a little bit impatient in the final third. "We were too impatient and eager.
body: "We were too impatient and eager. It was a little bit up and down. In the second half we moved the ball quicker and switched from left to right and we saw the confidence grow.

" Liam Delap 's hit didn't surprise me because I see it in training. That's what a striker should do. I feel this goal gave him a lot of confidence because he was a lot more present. It was a top team performance."

Nottingham Forest striker Igor Jesus, who scored the 88th-minute winner: "It's our first win in the Premier League this season and we know how important it is for us. It's very important for us and we need to keep it going. I just want to say thank you to everyone who came to support us today."
Four of Liam Delap's 14 Premier League goals have come against Aston Villa, his most against a single opponent in the competition.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Big fan of Forty Years On in Sceptre Stakes
articles.summary: Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle previews the final day of the St Leger Festival at Doncaster - live on Sky Sports Racing – alongside top-quality action on Champions’ Weekend at The Curragh.
body: I've made no secret of my admiration for FORTY YEARS ON who can make an instant impact in Pattern company when she contests the feature race at Doncaster on Sunday, the Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05).

George Scott, who won Friday's Doncaster Cup with Caballo De Mar, has found a great opportunity for this most progressive daughter of Mayson who was much too good for her rivals in a valuable handicap at Goodwood last month.

She enjoys ease underfoot and can win for the sixth time in eight starts at the possible expense of Shadwell's Touleen, who brings solid Group One form to the race after her luckless run in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot.

She did look a bit awkward in the Valiant Stakes last time so the cheekpieces may just sharpen her focus, while Planet Seeker looks over-priced on the strength of her York form and her creditable fourth in the Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola cannot axe 'fierce' Liverpool star again after what happened vs Fulham
articles.summary: Liverpool were held to a 0-0 draw against Fulham on Saturday afternoon. After coming off the back of two impressive wins against Ipswich and Atletico Madrid, fans probably expected a lot more from the Anfield outfit.
body: In fact, in both of those previous games, it finally felt like the Liverpool of old were making a return.
However, that was evidently not the case with Andoni Iraola's men barely able to string more than five passes together.

Of course, the former Bournemouth boss is still trying to figure out what his best starting XI is but, with the way that their performances have been going recently, it's clear that it's still going to take a while for them to get used to the new way of doing things.
And, for Iraola, this is all obviously still a learning curve as, he now won't want to drop one of his regular starters ever again after the performance his replacement put on display.

articles.title: 'No idea what to expect’ – F1 braced for Madring debut race mystery
articles.summary: George Russell believes Formula 1's first race at the Madring could swing one of two extreme ways, while Lewis Hamilton admits he does not know what exactly to expect, heading into Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.
body: The wall-lined circuit in Madrid has proved a big challenge for drivers so far on its inaugural weekend, while Friday's practice running showed up tyre degradation difficulties on long heavier-fuel runs.

The grid's leading drivers are braced for those challenges to continue into a 57-lap race for which McLaren's Lando Norris starts on pole position ahead of Mercedes' championship-leading Kimi Antonelli.
Mercedes' Russell, who qualified sixth after a disappointing Q3, told Sky Sports F1: "I think tyre degradation will define it one way or another.
"There will either be no degradation and it will be a procession, or really high degradation and it will be pretty chaotic."

articles.title: Norris beats Antonelli with 'masterpiece' to take Spanish GP pole
articles.summary: Lando Norris produced a stunning lap to beat Kimi Antonelli to the first pole position at Formula 1's all-new Madring circuit in a thrilling Spanish Grand Prix Qualifying.
body: The McLaren driver hadn't appeared to be in contention for pole at any point of the session, but found a huge amount of pace on his final run to edge out championship leader Antonelli by 11 thousandths of a second.

Max Verstappen, who had surged into pole contention earlier in the session, edged out Lewis Hamilton for third after the Ferrari driver produced a strong recovery having crashed in final practice earlier on Saturday.
Charles Leclerc starts behind his Ferrari team-mate in fifth, while Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate and nearest championship challenger, George Russell, could only manage sixth.
The remarkable nature of Norris' lap was further highlighted by a near-half second gap to his team-mate Oscar Piastri in seventh.
